issues.description: PersonResource constructor in the solution repository accepts a NoteService parameter and assigns personService to null, while the template and the problem statement expect PersonResource to be constructed with a PersonService. This mismatch will cause a null PersonService in the working solution (leading to runtime errors) and contradicts the template API students are asked to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the PersonResource constructor in the solution to accept a PersonService parameter and assign it to the final field. For example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; } Ensure the constructor parameter type matches the template and the expected dependency so the endpoints can call personService without NullPointerExceptions.

issues.description: PersonResource constructor parameter in the solution is named and typed as NoteService (de.tum.in.ase.eist.service.NoteService noteService) and sets the personService field to null. The template and the problem statement expect PersonResource to be constructed with a PersonService and forward requests to that PersonService. This mismatch breaks the conceptual mapping between the PersonResource and the PersonService (the core service the REST endpoints should delegate to) and will confuse students about which service the resource uses.
issues.suggestedFix: In the solution, change the PersonResource constructor to accept a PersonService and assign it to the field, matching the template and the problem description. Example: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; } Also remove the incorrect NoteService parameter and ensure imports/reference types refer to PersonService.
